newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Mining sees flat 1997/98 capital investment.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Mining sees flat 1997/98 capital investment.

text.p: Nippon Mining and Metals Co said on Wednesday it planned capital investment of 10 billion yen in fiscal 1997/98, unchanged from the previous year.

The majority of the investment, or 5.2 billion yen, was earmarked for the copper and chemicals division, followed by 1.9 billon yen for metal processing and 1.3 billion yen for zinc and precious metals division, the company said in a statement.
A spokesman at Nippon Mining said the company had no intention of increasing its copper production capacity beyond a plan released earlier this year.

In January, Nippon Mining said it would boost its copper smelting capacity by 70,000 tonnes to 420,000 tonnes per year and electrolytic copper refining capacity by 40,000 tonnes to 390,000 tonnes per year by 1999. The firm estimated the total cost of the expansion at 5.5 billion yen.

Of the 10 billion yen to be spent in 1997/98, 5.5 billion would be spent on raising production capacity and rationalising facilities, while 4.5 billion yen would be used for maintainance, the company said.
